## stella-protocol/src/event.rs
    3  //! `--output-format stream-json` is a `serde_json` serialization of this
    4  //! exact enum, one line per event: a stable, versioned machine interface.
    5  //!
    6  //! The vocabulary is additive-only: later variants are appended as the
    7  //! context/media/fleet crates land, never a breaking rename.
    8  //!
    9  //! "Additive" is directional, but both directions are now survivable. New
   10  //! *fields* ride `serde(default)`, so a newer reader parses every older
   11  //! stream. New *variants* travel backwards through
   12  //! [`AgentEvent::Unknown`]: an unrecognized `"type"` deserializes into that
   13  //! variant with the original JSON object preserved whole in `payload`, and
   14  //! re-serializes without losing a key or a value. An older binary therefore
   15  //! *skips* an event from the future instead of failing the whole stream.
   16  //!
   17  //! Round-tripping an unknown event preserves its *content*, not its exact
   18  //! bytes: [`serde_json::Value`] holds object keys in a `BTreeMap`, so they
   19  //! come back sorted rather than in their original order. JSON object key
   20  //! order carries no meaning (RFC 8259 §4), so nothing downstream may depend
   21  //! on it — but a consumer diffing raw lines should compare parsed values.
   22  //!
   23  //! The backwards direction is variant-shaped, not field-shaped, and the
   24  //! difference is easy to over-read. A *known* tag carrying a field this build
   25  //! has never heard of parses fine — serde ignores unrecognized keys — but that
   26  //! field is gone the moment the event is re-serialized, because nothing
   27  //! captured it. A proxy or `replay::to_jsonl` relaying a newer stream
   28  //! therefore passes new *events* through whole and silently narrows new
   29  //! *fields* on events it already knows. Only [`AgentEvent::Unknown`] preserves
   30  //! an object verbatim; capturing stray keys on the typed variants would take a
   31  //! `serde(flatten)` overflow map on each one, and no variant carries one.
   32  //!
   33  //! The tolerance is deliberately narrow, and the line matters: the fallback
   34  //! fires **only for an unrecognized tag**. A *recognized* tag whose body does
   35  //! not match its variant is still a hard error, because that is a real
   36  //! encoder bug or a corrupt record — silently degrading it to `Unknown` would
   37  //! turn data corruption into a shrug. See [`KNOWN_TYPE_TAGS`].
   38  //!
   39  //! Note this makes `AgentEvent`'s `Deserialize` impl specific to
   40  //! self-describing formats (it buffers through [`serde_json::Value`] to read
   41  //! the tag before dispatching). That is the format this type has always been
   42  //! defined against — `--output-format stream-json` *is* `serde_json` — so the
   43  //! constraint costs nothing in portability. It does cost work: every decode
   44  //! materializes the whole event as a [`serde_json::Value`] first, so a body's
   45  //! strings are allocated twice on the way in. That is paid on the journal
   46  //! replay path, not on the live emit path (serialization is unaffected), and
   47  //! it is the price of reading the tag before dispatching without hand-writing
   48  //! a visitor per variant.
